text:
maya: heads-up — ap-sg dedicated pool 'pool-delta' at 98% GPU allocation, admission controller flipped to rate-limit low-priority requests ~2m ago, seeing 429/admit-rejected logs. dashboard: https://internal.monitoring/pool-delta
infra-oncall: on it, pulling cluster health now
ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0423-APSG-POOL-SPK by @maya
samir: tailing qmgr on host-gpu-12, lots of queue growth and large batch sizes from a single stream
maya: can we open temporary burst capacity or reroute best-effort traffic to fallback pool?
julia: we have ~8 spare GPUs in eu-west; cross-region routing ok but adds ~120-200ms latency for some customers
lee: priority: protect committed customers. proposal: 1) enable burst for committed pool for 5m, 2) reroute best-effort to fallback-model (small-quant), 3) throttle noisy tenant
kai: I can toggle the burst flag. API: `curl -X POST "https://infra-api/flags/burst?pool=pool-delta&enable=true"`
ash: logs show tenant t-883 sending huge batches (token=>50k across requests) — likely the spike source
samir: confirmed noisy tenant. will apply a concurrency cap at LB for that tenant
maya: samir — how will you cap?
samir: applying nginx rule now: `limit_req zone=heavy burst=2 nodelay` on /v1/dedicated/pool-delta for tenant t-883
ops-bot: change: nginx rate-limit rule applied by samir @ 1859991092
kai: toggled burst flag for pool-delta @ 1859991185; flag active for committed-tier only
deploy-bot: routing change: diverted 20% of best-effort traffic to eu-west fallback at 1859991203, 3 hosts drained from pool-delta
julia: metrics: queue length -> 50% in 60s, 429s dropped from 300/min to 40/min, latency p95 unchanged for committed customers
maya: still seeing one host with GPU mem fragmentation and elevated GC; planning a graceful restart of inference-worker-12
lee: scheduling restart now with drain and live-migrate KV cache, ETA 6m
ash: added temporary slow-down rule for t-883: concurrency=1 and batch-size cap 512
samir: post-action logs show reduced batch spikes from t-883, admission backpressure relieved
maya: good work. keeping this thread open for 30m to watch stability. next steps: patch admission controller to detect batch-size storms and pre-throttle noisy tenants
infra-oncall: filing incident report and assigning SRE/PM for postmortem (INC-2026-0423). will include timeline and mitigation steps
maya: +1 on postmortem. add follow-up tasks: 1) auto-detect batch-size anomalies, 2) safe burst gating per-tenant, 3) telemetry on queue-length per-pool
lee: will open RFC for safe-burst gating and cross-region spillover cost impact assessment
maya: will close thread once stable for 20m, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
infra-oncall: incident noted as mitigated at 1859991435 — monitoring continues
